newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's ASLK stake could be part-listed -FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's ASLK stake could be part-listed -FinMin.

text.p: The Belgian cabinet on Friday approved a draft law on the sale of about half of the state's equity stake in ASLK/CGER Bank and ALSK/CGER Insurance on Friday while leaving open the option of a partial bourse listing.
A statement after the weekly cabinet meeting said the approval cleared the way for talks with ASLK's private sector shareholder, Fortis, with a view to the transfer of the state's 24.7 percent stake.
The stake is split into a 9.8 percent and a 14.9 percent portion. For each there is a different privatisation procedure.
Belgian-Dutch financial services group Fortis has an option on the 9.8 percent stake, which it got upon buying its current 49.9 percent holding in ASLK in 1993 for 35 billion francs.
For the remaining portion there is a tender procedure, open to any bidder, after which the government will set a selling price, a Finance Minister spokeswoman told Reuters.
Fortis has the right of first refusal. "Fortis can say that they want to buy at that price. If that does not happen, a bourse listing is an option," she said.
She gave no further details on the procedure.
The state's FPM/SFP holding company currently has 49.9 percent of ASLK. After the sale it will have 25.1 percent, the minimum required by Belgian law.
ASLK Bank and ASLK Insurance each hold 0.1 percent of the group's shares.
The cabinet's decision marks the formal start of negotiations.
In March Paul Van Rompuy, director of FPM/SFP, already said both sides were awaiting suggestions from the state privatisation committee about how the sale could be realised.

Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt favours a listing because it would give the government a reference framework for the price, because otherwise ASLK would be the only one of the five major banks not be listed and finally because it would be "a good operation" for Brussels as a financial centre.
